I need to design 3 example grids with noise pixels, framed holes, and matching hole shapes, making sure noise colors don't accidentally form valid frames and hole colors don't appear elsewhere by mistake. I'm starting with a 12x12 grid using noise colors 4 and 8, hole color 0, and frame color 5, sizing the hole carefully to avoid ambiguity.

Now I'm working on a second grid with a different hole shape, keeping the same constraints for the frame.

Filling in the rest of the grid rows, placing the framed hole at row3 cols2-4 and starting the second 1x3 zero run at row8 col8, keeping the noise pattern of 3s and 6s consistent elsewhere.

Now moving to grid 3, a 14x14 layout with noise values 1 and 7, frame value 3, and hole value 0, with a 2x2 hole framed at rows1-4/cols1-4 and two other target regions to place at rows7-8/cols3-4 and rows10-11/cols9-10. I'm laying out the alternating noise rows to build this grid.

Continuing the grid rows down through row13, I locate the frame at rows10-11 cols9-10 forming a ring at rows9-12 cols8-11, and I check the third grid's frame color 3 only appears as an outline as expected. Everything checks out, so I'm ready to submit all three grids.
